Single Inheritance: A subclass inherits from only one superclass. This is the most basic form of inheritance. Example: Class Dog inheriting from class Animal. 2. Multilevel Inheritance: A subclass inherits from another subclass, creating a chain of inheritance. Example: Class Puppy inheriting from Dog, which inherits from Animal. 3. Hierarchical Inheritance: Multiple subclasses inherit from a single superclass. Example: Classes Dog and Cat both inheriting from Animal. 4. Multiple Inheritance (through interfaces): A class can inherit from multiple interfaces, allowing it to implement methods from different sources. Java does not support direct multiple inheritance of classes. Example: Class implementing interfaces Runnable and Comparable. 5. Hybrid Inheritance: Combines different types of inheritance, typically using class hierarchies and interfaces. Example: A class inheriting from a class and implementing multiple interfaces.
